title: Where does the compass tip go for a body top that dips?
description: A person is drawn from a circle for the head, a short neck line and a rectangle body whose top edge curves downwards. The video places the compass tip above the body so the arc dips in the middle. Keeko raises the doubt that the tip must sit on the figure itself.
teaching_notes: One idea: an arc that dips in the middle is drawn with the tip above the figure, not on it. Watch for the slip of placing the tip inside the body, which gives an arc that bulges upward.

source: Draw a person made of a circle for the head, a short straight neck line below it, and a body that is a rectangle whose top edge is a curved arc dipping in the middle. How will you draw the curved top of the body with a compass? Where should the tip be placed and what radius should be used?
video_script.why: The child learns that a curved edge is part of a circle, so the compass tip may sit off the figure, and finds the tip by trial with a ruler.
video_script.substitution: A body six centimetres wide, with the tip four centimetres above the line joining the top corners.
video_script.anchor: A person drawn from a circle head, a short neck line and a body with a dipping top
video_script.wrong_answer: put the tip inside the body
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts the tip inside the body, on the figure itself. The arc then bulges upward like a hill, but the body top must dip in the middle, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The tip goes above the body, and the opening reaches both top corners.

final_answer.value: open ended; the head is a circle; the body top is an arc with the tip above the body on the line through its middle, and the opening is the distance from the tip to a top corner (for a body 6 cm wide: tip 4 cm above the top corners, opening 5 cm)
final_answer.spoken: the head is a circle, and the body top is an arc drawn with the tip above the body, in line with its middle, and an opening that reaches both top corners; for a body six centimetres wide the opening is five centimetres

never_show: the finished person before the answer
maths_rules: Head: a full circle drawn with the compass. Neck: a short straight line below the head.
Body: two vertical sides and a flat bottom; the two top corners are 6 cm apart, so each is 6 / 2 = 3 cm from the middle line.
The top edge is an arc of a circle joining the two top corners and dipping in the middle.
Tip on the middle line, 4 cm above the line joining the top corners; each top corner is then 5 cm from the tip (3-4-5 right triangle, checked with a ruler).
The lowest spot of the arc is 5 cm below the tip, which is 5 - 4 = 1 cm below the top corners.
Slip: a tip inside the body gives an arc that bulges upward, not one that dips.
video_script.design: One idea: an arc that dips has its tip above the figure, found by trial. Uses the half circles of the wave. Wrong idea: the tip must be on the figure. The person stays all video.
